title: Minimalist Onramp Micro-Illustrations and Screenshot Suite
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Produce a compact, low-fidelity-first set of onboarding assets for the Quickstart landing (we call the pattern 'Onramp'): hero variants, a 3-panel schematic diagram, micro-illustration tokens for the three starter steps, and a responsive screenshot suite (desktop, tablet, mobile). Goal is to reduce cognitive load for new users, speed up engineering integration, and enable A/B testing between an imagery-focused hero and a context-first hero. Deliver high-contrast accessible assets with export-ready slices for engineering and marketing.
deliverables: Hero - two main variants (Context-First: condensed copy + inset screenshot; Image-First: micro-illustration + short blurb)
3-Panel Schematic - single-line pipeline visual showing SDK -> Model -> Serve with lightweight animations (Lottie-ready simplified frames)
Micro-Illustration Set - 12 tokens (3 step states x 4 color/size variants) consistent with Redwood brand geometry
Step Cards - 3 modular step cards with icons, short copy, and checklist microcopy
Screenshot Suite - exported responsive screenshots for desktop/1280, tablet/768, and mobile/375 with safe area overlays
Figma file with componentized symbols and a developer handoff page with slice zips and CSS token recommendations
acceptance_criteria: All hero variants implemented in Figma with editable copy and component variants
PNG/JPEG exports delivered for all responsive breakpoints and retina scales (1x, 2x)
3-Panel schematic available as SVG and simplified Lottie frames
Design tokens (colors, spacing, typography scales) documented in the Figma handoff page
Contrast checks pass WCAG AA for normal text and large text; assets include a high-contrast alt-mode
Engineering integration checklist completed and reviewed by frontend eng owner
decisions: Chose minimalist geometry language over illustrative scenes to reduce localization friction and render complexity
Default hero will use 'Context-First' variant for GA to prioritize clarity in first-run conversion tests
Micro-illustration tokens will be single-color masks with accent fills to ease theming across dark/light modes
tradeoffs: Reduced detail in illustrations saves engineering and export time but may lower initial emotional appeal; plan to test with marketing-led variant later
Using SVG + CSS tokens increases frontend flexibility but requires an upfront engineer hookup for theming variables
Animations are simplified Lottie frames to avoid large bundle sizes; full vector motion deferred to Q3 if performance budget allows
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial concept sketches complete (3 hero directions). Posted to Slack #design-onboarding for feedback.
2025-02-18: Narrowed to 2 hero variants after PM feedback; created component anatomy and copy-length guidelines.
2025-02-24: Figma components built and token page scaffolded. Started responsive screenshot exports.
blockers: Frontend engineering availability for CSS token integration (blocked by ENG-2741 resource contention)
Need final hero headline copy from marketing for GA assets (pending PM sign-off)
Access to the staging product instance for mobile screenshots (request submitted to infra)
review_comments: PM - Alex Rivera: 'Love the reduced copy direction; please ensure the hero CTA maps to existing signup flow so we don't fragment analytics.'
Eng - Priya Nair: 'SVGs look good; add a fallback raster for older Android webviews. Also prefer exported CSS variables rather than hard-coded color values.'
Design Lead - Omar Bekele: 'Micro tokens are on-brand but increase stroke widths at small sizes for legibility. Provide 16px and 24px icon variants.'
engineering_notes: Frontend owner: Lukas Ortega - will allocate 2 dev days in Cycle 2025-W10 for token hookup and image slices.
Integration ticket created: ENG-2890 - Onramp hero integration and responsive snapshots.
Performance check: hero image budget target < 80KB gzipped; Lottie simplified frames aim for < 40KB each.
metrics_and_observability: Primary metric: Quickstart CTA CTR on landing page (baseline 6.2%)
Secondary metric: Time-to-first-successful-API-call on Quickstart guide (baseline 48s)
A/B test planned: Context-First vs Image-First hero (start week 2025-W11)
handoff_instructions: Engineers: import the tokens.css file attached in the figma handoff frame and wire up :root variables
Provide alt text drafts in the Figma handoff page; marketing will finalize copy for GA
notes: Localization: avoid embedded text within illustrations; place copy outside artboards to ease translation
Accessibility: include a high-contrast alt-mode variant for low-vision testing and a keyboard-focus visual state for the hero CTA
Future: consider animated token flow between SDK and Serve for a short explainer video (Q3)
final_steps: Resolve frontend integration comments and merge PRs
Run A/B experiment and collect 2 weeks of data
Prepare launch checklist for marketing and support with final asset pack
